title: Multiplicity adjustment: Holm, Hochberg and Benjamini-Hochberg
summary: Adjusted p-values for a family of ten secondary outcomes, controlling the family-wise error rate (Holm, Hochberg) or the false discovery rate (Benjamini-Hochberg).

sizing._note: Size each outcome at the adjusted alpha it will be tested at (for Bonferroni-type control, alpha / m).

pinned_defaults: Welch's t-test per outcome; R p.adjust(method = 'holm' / 'hochberg' / 'BH'); Python statsmodels multipletests(method = 'holm' / 'simes-hochberg' / 'fdr_bh').
The family (ten secondary outcomes) and the error rate are named before looking.
_which: Holm controls the family-wise error rate under any dependence; Hochberg is more powerful but needs independence or positive dependence; Benjamini-Hochberg controls the false discovery rate. Over 100 seeds, testing the seven null outcomes unadjusted rejected at least one 30% of the time, Holm 6%, BH 13% (BH does not control FWER, by design).
